patterns.title: Rules now follow inventions within 1 year
patterns.subtitle: Rules since 2000 follow inventions they answer within 1 year, by median; before 2000 that median was 11.5 years. Years from invention, product or milestone to its first linked policy event, over 143 linked pairs, grouped by period of each rule

overview.t: Each dot is one policy event, meaning a law, rule or government program, that compilers linked to an earlier invention, product or milestone. Its position marks that rule's year and its height shows years elapsed.
Shortest gaps sit near zero:
Sputnik 1 launched
(1957) was followed within one year by
NASA established by the National Aeronautics and Space Act
One pair more than three centuries apart is left out as succession rather than answer.

patterns.exception: Edward Jenner tests cowpox inoculation against smallpox to World Health Assembly resolves to eradicate smallpox: 163 years
patterns.cannot: Links are compilers' judgments: 90 of 143 were drawn in 2020 or later, so early medians rest on few pairs. Missing links do not mean missing rules.

annotations.label: World Health Assembly resolves to eradicate smallpox: 163 years after Edward Jenner tests cowpox inoculation against smallpox
NASA established by the National Aeronautics and Space Act: same year as Sputnik 1 launched

patterns.title: After a disaster, a rule within two years
patterns.subtitle: 89 percent of rules linked to disasters arrived within two years; median gap is 0 years. Years from failure or incident to the policy event this record links to it, over 166 pairs, 1346 to 2026

overview.t: Each stem rises from its failure or incident year to the years that passed before its linked rule. Most stems are short: 147 of 166 pairs resolve within two years. Clearest cases are
Railway Mania peaks and collapses
The Limited Liability Act allows limited liability for companies
The first transatlantic cable failed after three weeks
International Telegraph Union is founded in Paris
Titanic sank after striking an iceberg
Radio Act of 1912 is signed into law

patterns.exception: 1948 Donora smog to Congress passes the Clean Air Act Amendments of 1970: 22 years
patterns.cannot: Failures that led to no rule are invisible here, and each link is one compiler's judgment: this record cannot tell whether that rule would have come anyway.

patterns.title: Four booms have turned to busts since 1967
patterns.subtitle: Booms in this record have turned to busts four times since 1967; falls take 3.5 years by median and recoveries 4 years. Yearly net sentiment, hope minus fear, over 189 items tagged bubble or hype cycle, 1344 to 2026, with each peak, trough and first positive year after it

overview.t: This band sums each year's sentiment scores, which compilers gave to items tagged bubble or hype cycle, meaning a wave of excitement about one technology. Hope plots above the line, fear below, smoothed over three years to find runs. 4 boom-to-bust turns appear.
Marvin Minsky predicts AI will be substantially solved within a generation
(peak 1967) gave way to
UK and DARPA cuts to AI research funding
; this series bottoms in 1972 and mood turns positive again by 1976.
Japan launches the Fifth Generation Computer Systems project
(peak 1981) gave way to
North American video game crash, symbolized by E.T. for the Atari 2600
; this series bottoms in 1983 and mood turns positive again by 1985.
Wired publishes “The Long Boom”
(peak 1997) gave way to
Dot-com bubble bursts after the Nasdaq peaks
; this series bottoms in 1999 and mood turns positive again by 2003.
IBM Watson wins the Jeopardy! competition
(peak 2011) gave way to
FTX cryptocurrency exchange collapses
; this series bottoms in 2026, with no recovery yet in the record.

patterns.exception: The 1972 trough took 4 years to recover
patterns.cannot: Scores are the compilers' readings; coverage of markets is much denser after 2015.

patterns.title: AI's share has dipped four times since 1943
patterns.subtitle: AI's share of this record has fallen into 4 troughs since 1943, about every 17 years. Only its 1978 trough falls in a conventional AI winter, meaning years when funding and interest in AI collapsed; it has not dipped since 2007. AI and precursor events as a share of all events per year, 1943 to 2026, seven-year smoothing, peaks and troughs detected on the smoothed line

overview.t: This line shows what share of all recorded events each year belong to AI or its precursors, smoothed over seven years. Growth of the corpus, meaning this whole collection of records, therefore does not count as a boom. Peaks fall in 1949, 1971, 1989, 2004 and troughs in 1955, 1978, 1997, 2007.
One of four troughs, 1978, falls inside conventional AI winters (1974 to 1980 and 1987 to 1993).
Its 1971 peak carries
DARPA funds the Speech Understanding Research program
Its 1989 peak carries
LeCun's convolutional network recognizes handwritten ZIP codes
Its 2004 peak carries
Mars rovers drive themselves
Its 1997 trough carries
Hochreiter and Schmidhuber publish the LSTM paper
Its 2007 trough carries
DARPA Urban Challenge won by Carnegie Mellon's Boss

patterns.exception: The share has climbed since 2012 without a trough, which may be a longer boom or a corpus compiled in 2026
patterns.cannot: A corpus compiled in 2026 over-represents recent years; the share corrects for volume only.

peak 1971: DARPA funds the Speech Understanding Research program
peak 1989: LeCun's convolutional network recognizes handwritten ZIP codes
peak 2004: Mars rovers drive themselves
trough 1955: Newell, Simon and Shaw develop the Logic Theorist
trough 1997: Hochreiter and Schmidhuber publish the LSTM paper

patterns.title: Labor and regulation, paired for six centuries
patterns.subtitle: Labor and regulation appear together in 25 events across 6 centuries, this record's longest-lived pairing. Pairs of themes tagged together on single events, over 138 pairings with at least six shared events and 60 themes

overview.t: Each arc joins two themes compilers tagged on one event; width counts shared events, and arcs are ordered by how long each pairing has persisted. Most common is regulation with safety, 140 events from
Locomotives Act 1865 imposes red flag rules
London's High Court upholds Ofcom's Online Safety Act data demands on Meta, TikTok and X
(2026). Longest-lived is labor with regulation, from
London's Weavers, the oldest livery company, receive a royal charter
noyb files five GDPR complaints against Scale AI over surveillance of its Outlier data workers

patterns.exception: platform-power with safety: 50 events, all since 2018
patterns.cannot: Tags are a 2026 vocabulary applied backwards, so medieval and early modern items carry few tags and old pairings are understated.

annotations.label: earliest labor + regulation: London's Weavers, the oldest livery company, receive a royal charter
latest regulation + safety: London's High Court upholds Ofcom's Online Safety Act data demands on Meta, TikTok and X

patterns.title: Military ideas reach open use in 14.5 years
patterns.subtitle: Military-born ideas reach open use in 14.5 years by median; lab results become products in 3 years by median. Years between linked events: 8 military-to-open-use links and 122 discovery-or-invention-to-product links

overview.t: Two strips of dots. On top sit 8 links from items tagged military in origin to later items in open use; below sit 122 links from discoveries or inventions to later products. Position marks years elapsed.
ENIAC announced to the public
(1946) led, after 5 years, to
UNIVAC I, the first US commercial computer, is accepted by the Census Bureau
First DARPA Grand Challenge ends without a finisher
(2004) led, after 16 years, to
Waymo begins full commercial robotaxi service in Phoenix
Gutenberg prints with movable metal type in Mainz
(1450) became
First Gutenberg Bible copies became available
after 4 years.
James Watt patents the separate condenser
(1769) became
Boulton and Watt engines enter commercial service
after 7 years.

patterns.exception: Banting and Best isolate insulin to Eli Lilly markets recombinant human insulin Humulin: 61 years
patterns.cannot: Crossings that were never linked are invisible, and the short lags of the 2020s partly reflect how densely the compilers linked recent items.

patterns.title: Half of US homes in 6.2 years since 1990
patterns.subtitle: Technologies that reached 10 percent of US homes before 1950 took a median 13.7 years to reach half; those arriving since 1990 took 6.2 years. Years from 10 to 50 percent of US households against the year 10 percent was reached, 18 technologies (Our World in Data)

overview.t: Each dot is one technology from Our World in Data's US household adoption series, placed at its year of crossing 10 percent of homes. Height shows years it then took to reach half. Arrival one decade later shortens that wait by about 1.8 years. Slowest was the landline telephone (43 years, from 1903); shortest was the smartphone (1.6 years, from 2011).

patterns.exception: Radio: 5.7 years from 1925; Dishwasher: 29.3 years from 1963
patterns.cannot: US households only; this source starts most old series at 10 percent, and smartphone and social media series count adults, so comparison is indicative.

patterns.title: Hope and fear have flipped once since the 1920s
patterns.subtitle: This record's mood has flipped between net hope and net fear once since the 1920s; its most fearful decade is the 2020s (mean −0.19). Compilers' sentiment score on 1540 hopes, fears and cultural items, by year and by decade, 1070 to 2026

overview.t: Bars count hopeful items above zero and fearful ones below for each year; dashed line marks each decade's mean score, from −2 to +2. Mood crosses that line once. Most hopeful: the 1920s (mean +0.77), led by
Fleming observes penicillin’s antibacterial effect
; most fearful: the 2020s (mean −0.19), led by
WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic
Its latest turn came between 2000 to 2009 (+0.59) and 2010 to 2019 (−0.08).

patterns.exception: The 2020s carry 693 scored items against 26 for the 1920s, so early decades swing on a handful of voices
patterns.cannot: Scores read what was written and kept; decades with fewer than ten items are drawn but not counted.

annotations.label: 1928: Fleming observes penicillin’s antibacterial effect
2020: WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic

patterns.title: 9 regions, age by age
patterns.subtitle: In 1026 to 1450 the largest band is Europe, 35 percent of located events among 9 regions; in 2017 to 2026 it is North America, 65 percent among 9 regions. Share of events by world region within each age of this millennium, over 3429 events carrying a region

overview.t: Each column is an age of the millennium; its bands are the share of located events in each world region. 3429 events carry a region.
In 1026 to 1450 the largest band is Europe, 49 of 141 located events across 9 regions, for example
Liber Abaci introduces Hindu-Arabic numerals in Europe
In 1450 to 1760 the largest band is Europe, 91 of 155 located events across 9 regions, for example
Gutenberg prints with movable metal type in Mainz
In 1760 to 1914 the largest band is Europe, 136 of 291 located events across 9 regions, for example
The Industrial Revolution transforms manufacturing
In 1914 to 1990 the largest band is North America, 527 of 839 located events across 9 regions, for example
Westinghouse broadcasts presidential election returns
In 1990 to 2017 the largest band is North America, 289 of 462 located events across 9 regions, for example
Human Genome Project launched
In 2017 to 2026 the largest band is North America, 1007 of 1541 located events across 9 regions, for example
Asilomar AI Principles developed at Beneficial AI conference

patterns.exception: 1026 to 1450, the most dispersed age: the leading region holds only 35 percent and 9 regions appear
patterns.cannot: Regions follow the sources the compilers could read, which favour Europe and North America; silence is not absence.
